headline: Discussed allowing long-term care facilities in Medium-Scale Neighborhood district; staff asked to study commercial use thresholds.
summary: The discussion covered whether to allow long-term care facilities in the Medium-Scale Neighborhood zoning district, where they are now allowed only in the Transit Overlay district. No vote was recorded on that question. Staff will explore changes to commercial use thresholds and bring back a recommendation.

decision_titles: Thresholds and maximum scale of commercial uses
plain_text:
PAGE 1 
SOUTH BURLINGTON PLANNING COMMISSION 
22 SEPTEMBER 2026 
 
The South Burlington Planning Commission held a regular meeting on Tuesday, 
September 22, 2026, at 7:00 p.m., in Room 301, City Hall, 180 Market Street, and 
via Zoom. 
 
MEMBERS PRESENT: J. Louisos, Chair; M. Mittag, D. MacDonald, D. Leban, C. 
Lawrence, M. Emery 
 
ALSO PRESENT: P. Conner, Director of Planning and Zoning; K. Peterson, City 
Planner, R. Doyle 
 
1. Instructions on exiting the building in case of an emergency: 
 
Ms. Louisos provided instructions on emergency exit from the building. 
 
 
2. Agenda: Additions, deletions or changes in order of agenda items: 
 
No changes were made to the agenda. 
 
3. Open to the public for items not related to the Agenda: 
 
No issues were raised. 
 
4. Announcements and staff report 
 
Staff provided updates on city projects to the Planning Commission.  
 
5. Long-Term Care Facilities and Commercial Use Scales in Medium-Scale 
Neighborhood District
PLANNING COMMISSION 22 SEPTEMBER 2026 PAGE 2 
The Planning Commission held a discussion of whether or not to allow Long-Term 
Care facilities in the Medium-Scale Neighborhood zoning district. Currently, Long-
Term Care facilities are allowed in the MSN in the Transit Overlay district. 
Commissioners discussed the pros and cons of allowing this use where transit is 
sporadic (approximately once per day per direction), the local and regional needs 
for this kind of facility, whether to apply limitations on the scale of the building(s) 
or variety of housing types, and what the impact of the use would be on the area. 
Commissioners also discussed how inclusionary housing requirements could be 
met in the business model of long-term care facilities.  
 
The Planning Commission also discussed if the thresholds between commercial 
uses or the maximum scale of commercial uses should be adjusted. The 
Commission tasked Staff with further exploring this and bringing back a 
recommendation.  
  
6. Development Trends and Implementation of recent LDR amendments 
 
Staff presented an update on development trends in South Burlington and 
potential early results from LDR amendments passed in the last few years.  
 
7. Update on the FY27 Work Plan 
 
Staff presented the FY27 Work Plan and progress updates from the first quarter of 
the fiscal year.  
 
8. Other Business 
9. Adjourn 
 
 
As there was no further business to come before the Commission, the meeting 
was adjourned by common consent. 
 
 
 
    ___________________________________ 
     Clerk
